blocks.text: This chapter presents Saul’s kingship as granted by the LORD: Samuel anoints him, God empowers him, and the people are shown the one the LORD has chosen. At the same time, the account does not treat having a king as freedom from obligation; monarchy remains accountable to fearing, serving, and obeying the LORD.

Read within 1 Samuel 8–12, Saul’s selection is held alongside the book’s severe criticism of Israel’s request for a king. The larger account therefore presents monarchy as permitted and accountable within Israel’s covenant life, rather than as simply good or simply evil.
